newsitem.title: USA: Dollar falls as Germany holds rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Dollar falls as Germany holds rates steady.

text.p: The dollar fell against the German mark Thursday as Germany's currency rallied after the Bundesbank held interest rates steady.
The dollar also fell against the Japanese yen but rose against other major currencies.

The council of the German central bank, or Bundesbank, voted at a meeting Thursday to hold rates steady, confirming public comments a day earlier by Bundesbank officials saying they saw no reason to expect lower rates ahead.
Lower rates in Germany would spur the sluggish German economy but would also tend to weaken the mark in the short run by reducing returns on mark-based assets.
"The Deutschemark should continue to strengthen, since now they don't expect a rate cut in Germany," said Dori Schwartz, associate international economist at Donaldson Lufkin and Jenrette.
The mark also regained ground lost to other currencies recently.
The dollar fell to 1.5175 marks late in New York from 1.5215 late on Wednesday. It also slipped to 112.82 Japanese yen from 112.95.
The British pound edged lower to $1.5955 from $1.5967. The dollar rose to 1.2557 Swiss francs from 1.2540 and climbed to Canadian $1.3453 from C$1.3438.
Perhaps the most dramatic recent move in currency markets has been the mark rally to 74.36 yen, its highest point in 44 months.
Japanese investors have poured money into overseas markets, notably Germany, in an effort to capture higher returns than those offered by meagre-yielding Japanese securities.
As a result, the mark has risen sharply against the yen, dollar and other European currencies.

"We're seeing overall mark strength. There is still a lot of disinvestment coming out of Japan into Europe, apparently into the mark first," said James Powers, corporate foreign exchange vice president at Westdeutsche Landesank Girozentrale in New York.
Meanwhile, the dollar spent most of the session parked just below 113 yen, bolstered by the yen's relative weakness against the mark.
Late in New York trading the dollar fell below 1.52 marks after holding near that level for most of the day.

Traders had cited solid buying interest from U.S. corporations and possibly European central banks for stabilising the dollar at 1.52 marks. When that support gave way, speculators quickly pushed the dollar to 1.5160 marks, its low for the day.
"There doesn't seem to be tremendous interest in buying dollars, it's more buying and selling marks," said Jeffrey Yu, senior currency dealer at Sanwa Bank in New York.
Traders noted the dollar stayed mostly in tight ranges Thursday after highly volatile trading in recent sessions.
Should the currency make a serious move either above 113 yen or below 1.5150 marks, key technical levels, heavy follow-up movement will likely ensue.
"If the dollar goes either way, you're probably going to see some heavy action," Mr. Powers said.
